# Description

This form provides for the reporting of operational and catch data from pole and line fisheries under the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme (ROS). The form is designed to capture verified information on fishing activity, catch composition, and bycatch associated with pole and line operations, including IOTC species, and other bycatch species.The reporting format follows the standards adopted by the IOTC Scientific Committee and includes multiple hierarchical data levels, ranging from trip and set information to species-specific catch and bycatch records. Data collected through this form contribute to scientific assessments of tuna and tuna-like species and support monitoring of the impact of pole and line fisheries on associated and dependent species. Observers are required to complete the form for pole and line operations covered by the ROS, ensuring consistency, transparency, and quality of the data collected.

REPLACE WITH PROPER FORM LINK     Click [here](./Form-1RC.xlsx) to download a blank version of the ROS-PL form, or [return](./index.html) to the list of all IOTC statistical data reporting forms.

# Data content

REPLACE WITH POLE AND LINE DESCRIPTION:   Total live weight of retained catches by species, along with information on the value (%) and type of sampling coverage used for the estimations by  quarter if available, year, fleet, fishery, retain reason and IOTC main area.

## Observer trip details

| **Embarkation:** Record the starting port. If the first observation is available after the departure form the port while the vessel is within port limits, this is still recorded as the observation starting port. If the observation starts at sea outside port limits (onboard observer boarding the vessel via a vessel transfer or EM records not available at the trip starting date due to a recording failure) , record “at sea”.

# Reporting deadlines

- **Longline fisheries**: 30 June (preliminary), 30 December (final)
- **Surface fisheries**: 30 June (final)
- **Coastal fisheries**: 30 June (final)
